value: Kakheti's main white grape, grown along the Alazani valley and the base of appellations such as Tsinandali, Gurjaani and Tibaani. It is made both as a pressed white and as an amber wine fermented on its skins in qvevri.
source_notes: georgia.travel (Georgian National Tourism Administration): Rkatsiteli a symbol of Kakheti, best from slopes around the Alazani valley, used in PDOs incl. Gurjaani, Vazisubani, Tibaani, Tsinandali; qvevri skin contact vs European method steel. Tsinandali PDO specification (Sakpatenti registry, applicant National Wine Agency, hosted by UK gov): white Tsinandali at least 85 percent Rkatsiteli. Wine Folly: Kakheti known for traditional qvevri Rkatsiteli with amber hues from skin contact.

value: Fermented on its skins in Kakheti's qvevri, it turns deep gold to amber, with honeyed notes and a richer, more tannic texture than the region's pressed whites.
source_notes: Wine Folly: Kakheti qvevri Rkatsiteli shows rich amber hues, textured body, dried apricot, honey and walnut. georgia.travel: qvevri gives a heavier, richer taste with more tannins and a dark golden colour; European method gives a milder, lighter wine.

value: Kisi is one of the white grapes allowed for white and amber Kakheti wine, and the only grape of the Magraanis Kisi appellation around Magraani in Akhmeta, made there as a dry white or a dry amber wine.
source_notes: Kakheti (Kakhuri) PDO specification (applicant National Wine Agency): white and amber Kakheti made from Rkatsiteli, Kakhuri Mtsvane, Kisi, Khikhvi, Mtsvivani Kakhuri, Chitistvala. Magraanis Kisi PDO specification (applicant Magraani Wine, Akhmeta): only Kisi, only white dry and amber dry, micro zone in Akhmeta municipality. georgia.to (Tbilisi travel company): Magriaani produces dry white and amber wines from Kisi.

value: In Kakheti its pressed whites lean to apple, pear and meadow flowers, while its qvevri amber wines turn fuller and gently tannic, gaining dried apricot and almond as they age.
source_notes: Magraanis Kisi PDO specification: white has meadow flowers, apple, pear, peach and citrus; amber is full, velvet, moderately tart, apple pear peach when young, almond and dried apricot with ageing. Madloba (Georgian catalogue site): European style Kisi shows pear, citrus, green tea; qvevri style more apricot, mango, orange and walnut.

value: In Kakheti it gives soft, fragrant whites with peach and other yellow fruit over a moderate acidity.
source_notes: Akhmeta / Akhmetis Mtsvane PDO specification (applicant National Wine Agency): white has very intensive aromas of yellow fruit, peach, grapefruit and tropical fruit, soft, with moderate acidity. Vivino style page for Georgian Mtsvane Kakhuri: strong floral aroma with peach and apricot, medium body, balanced acidity.

value: Vayots Dzor's leading red grape and probably its birthplace, grown in high vineyards, many of them on their own roots. Wineries across Armenia buy Areni from here, and it is made as still red and as sparkling wine.
source_notes: Decanter (Armenia wine lover's guide): key grapes in Vayots Dzor are Areni for red and sparkling; many Armenian wineries buy grapes from Vayots Dzor; vines planted on own roots at high elevations. World of Fine Wine: Vayots Dzor seems both Areni's birthplace and the region best suited to it; producers across Armenia source it from the province.

value: Grown high on volcanic soils in a cool climate, it keeps lively acidity and silky tannins, and is often likened to a fuller Pinot Noir or a lighter, less extracted Grenache.
source_notes: Decanter: Areni compared to a fuller bodied Pinot Noir or slimmed down Grenache for red fruit, lively acidity and silky tannins; Vayots Dzor has volcanic soils and a cooler climate. World of Fine Wine: compared to brighter, less extracted Grenache; depth without heaviness; smoky mineral note from volcanic soils in better examples.

value: The main white grape of Vayots Dzor, where it does well in the cool, high vineyards.
source_notes: Decanter: key grapes of Vayots Dzor are Areni for red and Voskehat for white. World of Fine Wine: Voskehat does very well in the province; the cooler conditions support a more focused expression.

value: The cool conditions here give it a focused, clean style that keeps its texture without turning broad or oily.
source_notes: World of Fine Wine: Voskehat has weight and texture but the best avoid the broad or oily character, and the cooler conditions in Vayots Dzor support a more focused expression. Decanter: Voskehat produces clean and bright styles and savoury textural wines.

value: The backbone of many Bekaa red blends, partnered with Syrah and Merlot or with the older Cinsault and Carignan plantings.
source_notes: Decanter (Jefford, Bekaa beauties): grand vins are Cabernet blends with Syrah (Kefraya, Tourelles), Cabernet Merlot Petit Verdot (Ksara), Musar Cabernet with Cinsault and Carignan. Harpers Lebanon Report: Cabernet Sauvignon the most popular international red; typical blends Cabernet with Carignan and Cinsault, or with Merlot and Syrah.

value: Mostly blended with Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah in the Bekaa, and sometimes bottled on its own.
source_notes: Decanter (Jefford): Ch St Thomas grand vin based on Merlot, Cabernet and Syrah, and a pure Merlot made when vintage conditions permit; Ksara blend of Cabernet, Merlot, Petit Verdot. Harpers Lebanon Report: Ch St Thomas makes a premium Merlot; many reds are Cabernet, Merlot and Syrah blends.

value: Used across the Bekaa mostly in blends with Cabernet Sauvignon, and some wineries also bottle it on its own.
source_notes: Decanter (Jefford): Syrah Cabernet blends at Kefraya, Tourelles, Ixsir. Harpers Lebanon Report: a premium Syrah varietal matured in oak, and numerous Cabernet Syrah blends.

value: One of the Bekaa's long established Mediterranean grapes, often grown as bush vines and used in blends.
source_notes: Harpers Lebanon Report: Jesuits made the first dry red from Cinsault, Carignan and Grenache; bush vines still widely used in the Bekaa and protect thin skinned Grenache; Grenache appears in Rhône style blends. Decanter regional profile: Mediterranean varieties incl. Grenache widely planted; most production in the Bekaa.

value: The dominant red grape of the Judean Hills and the heart of the region's Bordeaux style blends.
source_notes: The Buyer: most grapes in the Judean Hills are red with Cabernet Sauvignon the dominant grape. Wine Spectator (Tasting in the Judean Hills): Castel makes Bordeaux style blends, Flam Classico is Cabernet and Merlot, Clos de Gat bottles Cabernet varietally.

value: Blended with Cabernet Sauvignon in the Judean Hills' Bordeaux style reds and also bottled on its own.
source_notes: Wine Spectator: Flam Classico blend of Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot; Flam and Clos de Gat (Har'el) bottle varietal Merlot. Jerusalem Post (Adam Montefiore): in the central mountains (Judea and Samaria) Merlot is the variety that shines.

value: One of the leading red grapes of the Judean Hills, made on its own and blended with Cabernet Sauvignon.
source_notes: Jerusalem Post (Montefiore): his choice for the Judean Hills is Syrah and Chardonnay; Clos de Gat Syrah first to gain notice. The Buyer: Syrah being planted in abundance; Tzora Cabernet Syrah blend; Flam Syrah dominant Superiore.

value: The leading white grape of the Judean Hills, made by some of its best wineries in a Burgundian style.
source_notes: Jerusalem Post (Montefiore): Judean Hills a fine region for whites, its Chardonnay as good as anywhere in Israel; C Blanc du Castel the most Burgundian. The Buyer: Chardonnay uppermost among whites; Castel C Blanc a Burgundian style Chardonnay.

value: Grown as one of the Judean Hills' whites after Chardonnay, bottled alone or blended with it.
source_notes: The Buyer: white experimentation with Chardonnay uppermost then Sauvignon Blanc; Tzora Shoresh Blanc 100 percent Sauvignon Blanc. Wine Spectator: Flam bottles an unoaked Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay blend.

value: The leading red grape of the Galilee's cool upland vineyards, especially in Upper Galilee, used alone and in Bordeaux style blends.
source_notes: Jerusalem Post (Montefiore): best varieties in Upper Galilee are the Bordeaux varieties, in particular Cabernet Sauvignon. WineTourism.com: Galilee vineyards on cool upland slopes, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Syrah the key reds.

value: One of the Galilee's most successful whites, grown in the cooler upland vineyards.
source_notes: Jerusalem Post (Montefiore): in the Galilee Sauvignon Blanc produces some of Israel's finest wines (Shvo, Tabor, Dalton, Yarden). WineTourism.com: Sauvignon Blanc among the main whites from cool upland slopes.

value: Chenin Blanc thrives in the high vineyards around Mitzpe Ramon and gives some of the Negev's most praised whites.
source_notes: Jerusalem Post (Montefiore): Mitzpe Ramon area the hub; main variety that shows well is Chenin Blanc, which seems to thrive there; Negev better for whites than reds. Washington Jewish Week: Nana near Mitzpe Ramon known for fresh, elegant whites, especially Chenin Blanc; many of the Negev's finest wines are whites incl. Chenin Blanc.

value: Grown on loess with cold desert nights, it keeps a striking freshness despite the heat.
source_notes: Washington Jewish Week: loess soils and cold nights give balance; Negev whites incl. Chenin Blanc show dazzling freshness despite the heat. Jerusalem Post (Montefiore): Chenin thrives in these high elevation vineyards.

value: Ripens well in the Negev and is used both in blends, notably with Malbec, and on its own.
source_notes: Jerusalem Post (Montefiore): Petit Verdot ripens well in Israel, a successful blending variety; Yatir varietal Petit Verdot and Ramat Negev show well in the Negev. Washington Jewish Week: Ramat Negev's Exodus Grand Reserve is a Petit Verdot and Malbec blend.

value: Used here in blends, notably with Petit Verdot.
source_notes: Washington Jewish Week: Ramat Negev's award winning Exodus Grand Reserve is a Petit Verdot and Malbec blend. Ramat Negev winery (producer's own site): Exodus Reserve made from Petit Verdot, Malbec and Cabernet Franc.

value: In Cappadocia it makes delicate, very pale, light bodied whites, sharpened by the cold nights of the high plateau.
source_notes: GoTürkiye (Turkish Ministry of Culture and Tourism): Emir wines delicate with exceptionally light colour; day and night swings at altitude and volcanic soil give high acidity and mineral tones. Decanter (Jefford, Turkish renaissance): Emir fragrant, summery, light boned; Cappadocia's high, continental conditions give finer grained wines with more sinew.

value: Often grown as old bush vines, especially on the sandy soils around Edirne, and made as red, rosé and traditional method sparkling wine.
source_notes: Wine Traveler: Papazkarası vineyards generally old bush vines on the sandy soils of upper Thrace around Edirne; makes fruity savoury medium bodied reds, crisp rosés, blanc de noir and traditional method sparkling. GoTürkiye: grown in Tekirdağ, Edirne and Kırklareli as a table grape and for red wine.

value: In Thrace it gives aromatic, medium bodied reds with high acidity and fairly light tannins.
source_notes: GoTürkiye: wine aromatic with medium low tannins and high acidity; plum, cherry, spice. Wine Traveler: fruity savoury medium bodied red wines.

value: One of the international grapes that lead Thrace's vineyards, grown around Kırklareli and Tekirdağ.
source_notes: GoTürkiye Thrace Vineyard Route: Cabernet Sauvignon listed among the foreign varieties grown in the Kırklareli and Tekirdağ areas. Wine Traveler: international grapes reign supreme in Thrace.

value: One of the international grapes that lead Thrace's vineyards, grown around Kırklareli and Tekirdağ.
source_notes: GoTürkiye Thrace Vineyard Route: Cabernet Franc listed among the foreign varieties grown in the Kırklareli and Tekirdağ areas. Wine Traveler: international grapes reign supreme in Thrace.

value: One of the international grapes that lead Thrace's vineyards, grown around Kırklareli and Tekirdağ.
source_notes: GoTürkiye Thrace Vineyard Route: Merlot listed among the foreign varieties grown in the Kırklareli and Tekirdağ areas. Wine Traveler: international grapes reign supreme in Thrace.

value: One of the international grapes that lead Thrace's vineyards, grown around Kırklareli and Tekirdağ.
source_notes: GoTürkiye Thrace Vineyard Route: Sauvignon Blanc listed among the foreign varieties grown in the Kırklareli and Tekirdağ areas. Wine Traveler: international grapes reign supreme in Thrace.

value: One of the international grapes that lead Thrace's vineyards, grown around Kırklareli and Tekirdağ.
source_notes: GoTürkiye Thrace Vineyard Route: Shiraz listed among the foreign varieties grown in the Kırklareli and Tekirdağ areas. Wine Traveler: international grapes reign supreme in Thrace.
